description: Founded in 1992, ScanSource, Inc is an international distributor of technology products and solutions, focusing on point-of-sale (POS), payments, barcode, physical security, unified communications and collaboration, cloud and telecom services.

press.summary: ScanSource, un fournisseur de services technologiques basé aux États-Unis, a été victime d'une attaque de ransomware qui a affecté certains de ses systèmes, opérations commerciales et portails clients. L'attaque a commencé le 14 mai 2023 et a entraîné des retards dans la fourniture de services aux clients en Amérique du Nord et au Brésil. L'entreprise a mis en place son plan d'intervention en cas d'incident et a alerté les autorités compétentes. Les experts en cybersécurité ont été appelés pour aider à minimiser les perturbations opérationnelles causées par l'incident. Il n'est pas encore connu quelle opération de ransomware est derrière l'attaque ou si des données ont été volées.

description: Hawa AG has been producing sliding solutions for creative building culture for more than 50 years. It is well-known as a premium provider of sliding fitting systems for equipment, room partitioning, shop fronts and facades.

press.summary: La société Hawa Sliding Solutions AG, fabricant suisse de ferrures pour portes coulissantes, a été victime d'une cyberattaque fin avril 2023. L'entreprise a immédiatement réagi en informant ses clients et fournisseurs, en coupant tous ses systèmes et en demandant à la plupart de ses employés de travailler depuis leur domicile. Une équipe interne et des spécialistes travaillent actuellement à la restauration complète des processus opérationnels. Les commandes ne peuvent actuellement être traitées que manuellement et les systèmes informatiques sont en cours de reconstruction. Les sites web de Hawa restent en ligne et les services clients sont accessibles par téléphone, e-mail et vidéoconférence.

press.summary: EDC informe ses clients qu'un groupe international de pirates informatiques a accédé à ses systèmes dans la nuit du mercredi 1er novembre 2023 et a volé un grand nombre de fichiers et de documents susceptibles de contenir des informations personelles.

description: REKORD ist meisterlicher Fachbetrieb für Fenster Sonderbau, Sprossenfenster und Denkmalschutzfenster. Damit können Sie sicher sein, ein handwerklich meisterhaftes und technisch perfektes Einzelstück zu erhalten. Eine Qualität, die bei uns von rekord seit über 100 Jahren gute Tradition ist. Unsere Produkte tragen das bekannte RAL-Gütezeichen für eine regelmäßige Qualitätskontrolle durch ein neutrales Institut. Darüberhinaus prüfen wir selbst vor dem Versand jedes einzelne Produkt noch einmal ganz genau, sorgfältig und umfassend anhand unseres Qualitätssicherheitssystems.SITE: www.rekord.de Address  Itzehoer Straße 10 25578 Dägeling DeutschlandFULL DATA SIZE: 917gb 1. Unternehmensdaten 2. Persönliche Daten 3. Projekte 4. CAD 5. Userdat

press.summary: Le fabricant de fenêtres et de portes Rekord Fenster Türen, basé à Dägelinger, a été la cible d'une cyberattaque le 1er novembre, ce qui a nécessité la mise hors ligne de tous ses systèmes. La direction estime que les pertes sont importantes mais se réjouit que l'attaque n'ait pas conduit à un arrêt total grâce à de bonnes mesures de protection déjà en place. Ils conseillent aux autres entreprises d'investir dans la sécurité informatique pour se prémunir contre de telles menaces à l'avenir.

L'hôpital Cogdell Memorial est confronté à un incident informatique qui bloque l'accès à certains de ses systèmes et perturbe fortement son réseau téléphonique, ce qui a entraîné la déconnexion de son réseau et l'adoption de processus manuels pour maintenir les services de routine. Ils collaborent avec des spécialistes en informatique et ont informé les autorités compétentes, tout en précisant qu'il n'y a pas encore de preuve d'utilisation frauduleuse des données, mais l'enquête est toujours en cours. L'hôpital conseille la vigilance face aux escroqueries potentielles et promet de communiquer des informations supplémentaires dès qu'elles seront disponibles.

description: DePauw University in Greencastle, Indiana, USA, is a private, national liberal arts college and School of Music. The school has a Methodist heritage and was originally known as Indiana Asbury University.

press.summary: L'Université DePauw a été victime d'une cyberattaque, entraînant une interruption des services internet et des e-services universitaires. L'incident a eu un impact considérable sur la vie étudiante, avec une interruption des cours en ligne, des services d'impression, des emails et du réseau local de l'université. Pour l'instant, on ignore si des informations privées d'étudiants ou d'employés de l'université ont été compromises.

description: British Library The British Library is a research library in London that is the national library of the United Kingdom. It is one of the largest libraries in the worl.

press.summary: La British Library a confirmé qu'une "cyberattaque" est à l'origine d'une panne informatique majeure qui dure depuis plusieurs jours. Cette attaque a affecté son site web, ses services sur place, y compris l'accès Wi-Fi, et a rendu presque tous leurs serveurs VMware ESXi indisponibles. Bien que la bibliothèque reste ouverte au public, elle n'accepte que les paiements en espèces et les services restants sont limités.

description: We engage our patients on a personal level. Every patient in our communities is a part of our Carespring family. We get to know them-their stories, their families, what the...

press.summary: Carespring Health Care Management, un fournisseur de soins de santé pour les personnes âgées, a subi une cyberattaque en octobre 2023, entraînant le vol de données sensibles de 67 000 individus. Une poursuite en justice allègue que l'entreprise a négligé ses obligations de sécurité, laissant ses informations exposées à des réseaux vulnérables. La plainte réclame des dommages et dénonce le retard dans la notification de la violation de données, qui n'a été envoyée qu'en août 2024.

description: Corsica Ferries - Sardinia Ferries - is a Franco-Italian ferry company that operates traffic to and from the islands of Corsica, Sardinia and Elba. Corsica Sardinia Ferries is the premier ferry operator on the Western Mediterranean Sea transporting more than 2.8 million passengers annually aboard their ferries running to and from France and Italy to Corsica, Sardinia and Elba.

press.summary: Le transporteur maritime Corsica Ferries a subi une cyberattaque, revendiquée par la franchise mafieuse Alphv, également connue sous le nom de BlackCat. Selon la revendication, 101 Go de données, incluant des informations financières, personnelles, des documents internes et des plans de navires, auraient été volés et téléversés sur les serveurs d'Alphv le 1er novembre. Toutefois, il n'est pas encore confirmé si des données de clients figurent parmi les informations volées.

description: Yamaha Motor Philippines,Inc. strives to realize people’s dreams with ingenuity and passion, a company that the community recognizes and counts on for the next electrifying innovation that provides...

press.summary: Yamaha Motor Philippines (YMPH) a été victime d'une cyberattaque le 25 octobre, lors de laquelle un serveur a été infecté par un rançongiciel et des informations personnelles des employés ont été partiellement divulguées. L'entreprise a signalé l'incident aux autorités philippines et travaille avec une équipe de contre-mesures et une société de sécurité Internet externe pour enquêter et prévenir d'autres dommages. Yamaha a confirmé que l'attaque était limitée à un serveur de YMPH et n'a pas affecté le siège social ou d'autres entreprises du groupe Yamaha Motor.

description: Nestled in the heart of East Toronto, Michael Garron Hospital (MGH), a division of Toronto East Health Network, is a vibrant community teaching hospital serving one of Canada’s most diverse communities. We have taken 882k files or 775 GB from their network. You will find lots of confidential information very soon. Stay tuned.

press.summary: L'hôpital Michael Garron est actuellement en train d'enquêter sur un "incident de sécurité des données" dont il a été informé récemment. Bien que les détails exacts de l'incident ne soient pas encore connus, l'hôpital a déclaré qu'il n'y avait "aucun impact connu" sur les applications cliniques ou les services de soins aux patients pour le moment. Cet incident survient dans un contexte où les établissements de santé sont de plus en plus la cible de cyberattaques, comme en témoignent les attaques par ransomware subies par le réseau de santé de Scarborough, l'hôpital pour enfants malades de Toronto et l'hôpital Humber River l'année dernière.

description: Advarra provides innovative regulatory compliance solutions and expertise throughout the research lifecycle. Our integrated end-to-end compliance management platform combines site training, protocol compliance, and patient engagement, plus experienced consultants available to assist your team.

press.summary: Advarra, une entreprise fournissant des solutions intégrées pour la recherche clinique, a été victime d'une cyberattaque le 25 octobre, au cours de laquelle des données ont été exfiltrées. Les auteurs de l'attaque ont menacé de divulguer les données, affirmant avoir obtenu plus de 120 Go de données confidentielles appartenant à des clients, des patients et des employés actuels et anciens. Advarra a répondu en déclarant qu'ils avaient pris des mesures pour contenir l'attaque et qu'ils croyaient que l'affaire était contenue, tout en continuant à enquêter avec des experts en cybersécurité tiers.

description: Bluewater Health is a hospital in Sarnia, Ontario.      The  hospital now encompasses about 600,000 square feet (56,000 m2). It employs almost 1,800 staff and physicians, along with over 700 volunteers, and is Sarnia—Lambton's largest public sector employer.

press.summary: Une cyberattaque a compromis plus de 30 ans de dossiers de patients dans plusieurs hôpitaux et sites de soins du comté de Lambton, affectant plus de 250 000 patients. Les informations volées incluent des noms, adresses, numéros de téléphone, dates de naissance et motifs de visites, ainsi que les numéros d'assurance sociale de 20 000 patients. Bluewater Health a mis en place une hotline pour répondre aux questions des patients concernés et contactera ceux dont les numéros d'assurance sociale ont été compromis.

description: The Museum für Naturkunde Berlin has a long and eventful history - it has seen days of glory and survived crises. The collections that were brought together over more than two centuries from all over the world created a treasure trove of knowledge.

In 1992, bicycle production in Brazil was only carried out by two large assemblers that divided the national market between themselves. Seeing the need for other options, Ciclo Cairu decided to enter the bicycle assembly market.
The company, which at the time had all the components necessary for assembling bicycles, began to assemble single-speed and geared mountain bikes, always assembled with top-of-the-line components. They were very well received, competing on equal terms with other national and imported brands.
In 1997, motivated by the Pirelli tire industry, which until then did not have a motorcycle tire distributor in the North region, the company took on yet another challenge of bringing that brand's tires to motorcycle stores and workshops. Knowing the segment, it realized the market opportunity for distributing motorcycle parts, and began selling motorcycle parts from several national and international manufacturers.
Today, Ciclo Cairu is a company that combines the distribution of bicycle and motorcycle parts with the industrialization of bicycles, offering competitive and high-quality products. Memorial Hospital and Manor celebrated its 50th Anniversary in 2010. Memorial Hospital was officially dedicated on Sunday, April 3, 1960, and opened its doors to receive patients the following day. The 80-bed hospital was built under the Hill-Burton Hospital Survey & Construction Act of 1946. The Hill-Burton Act initiated the concept of local, state, and federal cost sharing of healthcare facilities, and provided federal funds for construction and renovation of more than 9,000 medical facilities, particularly in lower income areas. While two-thirds of the money was provided by the Federal government and the State of Georgia, Memorial Hospital has always been operated by the Hospital Authority of the City of Bainbridge and Decatur County.

Prior to the opening of Memorial Hospital, two private hospitals served the healthcare needs of Decatur and surrounding counties. In 1916, Riverside Hospital was built and operated by Dr. J. D. Chason, Dr. Gordon Chason, Dr. R. F. Wheat, and Dr. Willie Lee Wilkinson. Shortly after the Riverside Hospital was built, Dr. A.E.B. Alford came to Bainbridge and built the Bainbridge Hospital. The Flint River provided easy access to these hospitals for people in rural areas and nearby towns, making Bainbridge a healthcare center for the tri-state area.  Memorial Hospital was given its name in memoriam to those pioneers who made Bainbridge the medical center of Southwest Georgia, Northern Florida, and Southeastern Alabama for many decades. - 1.15 TB Data

Horizon Family Medical Group  A deep dive into 7 terabytes of internal data: from patient records to QuickBooks financial databases  In the modern world, data is the new oil. For a medical organization like Horizon Family Medical Group, it is also the foundation of trust between doctor and patient. We have conducted an independent and complete audit of this organization's data security. The results are catastrophic. We are in possession of the company's entire digital footprint, totaling **7 terabytes**, which includes 1TB of file data and 6TB of mission-critical SQL and QuickBooks databases.  The management of Horizon Family Medical Group was notified of their complete loss of data control. They chose silence. This blog exists to illuminate what they are desperately trying to hide. We will not be publishing the files. Yet. Instead, we will explain exactly what this data contains, so that every patient, employee, and partner can appreciate the full scale of the threat.  The Patient, Dissected. What We Know About You  Horizon Family Medical Group prides itself on a wide range of services, from primary care to specialized treatments. This range of services has now become a detailed vulnerability map for every single patient. Our data includes, but is not limited to:  Primary Care: Complete visit histories, diagnoses, prescriptions, lab results, and physicians' private notes about your lifestyle, habits, and family status. Women's Health: Detailed information on gynecological exams, pregnancies, abortions, Pap smear results, STD diagnoses, and prescribed treatments. Everything you trusted only to your doctor. Behavioral Health: The most sensitive category. Diagnoses related to depression, anxiety disorders, bipolar disorder, and addiction. Full session notes from psychotherapists. Every antidepressant and antipsychotic prescription. This information can destroy careers, families, and social standing. Allergy and Immunology: Data on all your allergies, including reactions to specific medications. What happens when this information is lost or altered in your official medical file? Ophthalmology & Nutrition: Your eyeglass prescriptions, diagnoses like glaucoma and cataracts, as well as all your attempts to manage weight, documented eating disorders, and private recommendations from nutritionists.  This isn't just 'data'. This is your life, cataloged and ready for use.  Anatomy of a Business. A Financial Teardown of Horizon Family Medical Group  It's a paradox that clinics, while collecting mountains of information, often fail to see the real picture of their own business. We see it. The 6 terabytes of SQL and QuickBooks databases represent the complete financial and operational model of Horizon Family Medical Group.  We have analyzed:  SQL Databases: These contain complete patient information, doctor schedules, office utilization, patient flow, average revenue per department and per doctor. We know which doctor is profitable and which is a liability. We see every operational metric management uses to make decisions. QuickBooks Databases: This is the financial heart of the company. Every transaction, employee salaries (including hidden executive bonuses), tax reports, debts, loans, and settlements with insurance companies and suppliers. We can see the true profit margin of every service, the customer acquisition cost (CAC), and their lifetime value (LTV).  Horizon's management hasn't just lost patient data. They have lost complete control of their business. Any competitor with this information could dismantle their company by poaching their most profitable doctors and patients.  Eternal Memory. Why This Data Will Never Disappear.  Some believe a data breach is a temporary problem. In this case, it is not. We drew inspiration from the Arctic Code Vault project, where humanity's most critical code is preserved in permafrost for a thousand years.  Your 7 terabytes of data are no longer just files on a server. They have been prepared for archival and distributed storage. They will become a digital monument to the negligence of Horizon Family Medical Group. This data cannot be 'deleted'. It will exist forever, as proof that the company's leadership failed to protect what is most sacred—your health and your privacy.   To the management of Horizon Family Medical Group, we remind you: the clock is ticking. Your silence only magnifies the damage. Contact us. Your patients and your business deserve it.

# American Council on Education — Data Breach Disclosure

**Published:** September 30, 2026
**Data Publication Date: October 7, 2026**

---

> *ACE was given the opportunity to resolve this matter privately. Their leadership engaged in discussions, then chose to walk away without resolution. Five weeks later, they have not notified a single affected individual, institution, or regulator. That decision has consequences.*

---

## About ACE

The [American Council on Education](https://www.acenet.edu) (ACE) is the primary coordinating body for U.S. higher education. Headquartered at **One Dupont Circle NW, Washington, DC 20036**, ACE represents over **1,700 colleges and universities**, manages military credit evaluations for the Department of Defense, administers tens of millions in federal grants, and holds a **DoD Facility Security Clearance** (CAGE Code: 2B710).

ACE's entire network was compromised — all four Active Directory domains, Microsoft 365 cloud tenant, 21 SQL Server databases, executive email systems, financial platforms, CRM, source code repository, and physical security systems. **271 GB of data was exfiltrated.**

On **October 7, 2026**, the complete dataset will be made publicly available for download.

![CHM Logo](logo_color.svg)

**Organization:** Chicago History Museum (formerly Chicago Historical Society)
**Location:** 1601 N Clark Street, Chicago, IL 60614
**Website:** chicagohistory.org

**Data Volume:** 4 departments + AWS cloud infrastructure, 15+ years of records

---

## WHAT HAPPENED

Chicago History Museum's internal file server **and** AWS cloud infrastructure have been fully compromised. Sensitive data from four departments and the production cloud environment has been exfiltrated:

**From Internal File Server:**
- **IT Credentials** — AWS root keys, server passwords, BitLocker encryption keys, 20+ vendor portal logins in plaintext
- **Accounting & Finance** — 15 years of ADP payroll records (2006–2021), bank reconciliations, audit workpapers, ACH authorization documents
- **Human Resources** — Employee background checks containing Social Security Numbers, I-9 immigration documents, personal identity verification forms
- **Development / Institutional Advancement** — Board of Trustees home addresses, major donor pledge records ($4.4M+ in named donations), corporate funder relationships, donor CRM exports

**From AWS Cloud (Account 187824323586):**
- **Production Database** — Full access to Aurora MySQL containing the museum's website, 27,422 form submissions with visitor personal data
- **14 EC2 Servers** — Complete control of production, staging, and scaling infrastructure
- **S3 Backups** — 20 GB of website backups (146,000 files) — the only cloud backup
- **27,422 Public Records** — Names, emails, phone numbers, and personal details of museum visitors, event clients, school field trip contacts, donor applicants, interns, and volunteers collected over 7 years

---

## DATA SAMPLES

### 🔑 IT Credentials Exposed in Plaintext

AWS root account access keys, BitLocker disk encryption recovery key, and passwords for Adobe, Microsoft, Blackbaud (donor payment platform), Symantec, and 20+ grant portals including Boeing, ComEd, Exelon, MacArthur Foundation, SAM.gov, and City of Chicago.

*See: Screenshots 01–05*

### 👥 Board of Trustees — Home Addresses

Full names, home addresses, ZIP codes, and spouse names for 40+ members of the Board of Trustees, including prominent Chicago families residing in Lake Shore Drive, Winnetka, Lake Forest, Hinsdale, and Gold Coast neighborhoods.

*See: Screenshot 06*

### 💰 Donor Pledge Records — Named Amounts

Capital Campaign Endowment pledge details totaling $4,460,684 from Board of Trustees members, including individual named amounts ranging from $2,000 to $700,650. Corporate donors include Molex Inc., First Chicago NBD, LaSalle National Bank, Crate & Barrel, and Commonwealth Edison.

Notable: Donald Rumsfeld — $50,000 pledge documented.

*See: Screenshot 07*

### 📊 15 Years of Payroll Data

ADP payroll general ledger reports from 2006 through 2021 containing employee compensation details, benefit allocations, and salary breakdowns for all museum staff.

*See: Screenshot 08*

### 🔒 Employee SSN & Background Checks

Background check documents for 20+ employees including SSA-89 Social Security verification forms, I-9 immigration employment authorization documents, and personal identification records.

Under the Illinois Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA), this constitutes a reportable data breach requiring notification to the Illinois Attorney General and all affected individuals within 45 days.

*See: Screenshot 09*

### 🏗️ Complete IT Infrastructure

Server inventory (20 servers, VMware ESXi environment), full Cisco network topology (5 switches, 450+ patch panel mappings), VLAN architecture, external IP ranges, and firewall configuration. Multiple Windows Server 2003 systems still operational.

### 🏦 Banking Records & Prior Fraud

14 years of bank reconciliation files (BMO Harris, Northern Trust), ACH authorization lists, W-9 tax forms, and documentation of a prior ACH fraud incident in April 2015.

*See: Screenshot 12*

---

### ☁️ AWS Cloud — Full Infrastructure Control

Using the AWS root access keys found on the file server, we accessed the museum's entire cloud environment:

- **AWS Account 187824323586** — root-level access, no MFA
- **Aurora MySQL Production Database** — full DBA privileges with GRANT OPTION. Dumped 127 tables from the production site database and 119 tables from the staging database

- **6 S3 buckets** — 20 GB of website backups, CDN content, and encyclopedia resources
- **2 CloudFront distributions** — content delivery infrastructure
- **30 WordPress admin accounts** with password hashes extracted
- **MySQL port 3306 publicly accessible** with no IP restrictions — a textbook security failure

**This means we have the ability to shut down the museum's website, delete all cloud backups, and wipe the production database at any time. The museum's RDS instance has zero snapshots — deletion is permanent.**

# The Neighborhood Shop That Conquered a Nation’s Retail Landscape

## How a single family’s modest grocery store in Veles evolved into a 70-strong national network by proving that scale and community trust are not mutually exclusive.

In the retail industry, there is a persistent myth that to scale nationally, a brand must inevitably shed its local soul. The prevailing logic dictates that as a chain expands, the neighborhood warmth of its origins is replaced by sterile corporate efficiency, and the familiar faces behind the counter are swapped for standardized kiosks. But in North Macedonia, a retail network that now spans dozens of towns and employs over 850 people is quietly dismantling that assumption. They are proving that the secret to dominating a national market might just be remembering exactly what it feels like to run a single corner store.

## The Story

### A Dream in Veles

The year was 1988. The retail landscape of the Balkans was on the precipice of massive change, but in the town of Veles, the Doševski family was focused on a much smaller canvas. They opened a modest neighborhood shop—a traditional local grocery. At the time, it was not merely a business adventure; it was the physical manifestation of a family dream.

Starting a retail business in any era requires a leap of faith, but doing so with a clear vision for a future that had not yet arrived requires something more. The Doševski family possessed an unwavering belief in their community. They understood early on that a grocery store is not just a place to exchange currency for goods; it is a daily touchpoint in people's lives. By treating every customer not as a transaction, but as a neighbor, they laid a foundation of trust that no amount of corporate marketing could buy.

As the years passed, the knowledge gained from those early days behind the counter became their greatest asset. They learned the rhythms of the town, the preferences of the locals, and the exact meaning of relentless dedication to service. This deep, localized understanding allowed them to expand their horizons, opening several more sales facilities throughout Veles. They were no longer just a single shop; they were a local institution.

### The Capital Leap and the Turning Point

Growth, however, demands evolution. The quality of their offerings and the fierce loyalty of their buyers eventually pushed the family to take a significant strategic step: opening their first market in Skopje, the capital of North Macedonia. Moving from a regional hometown favorite to the highly competitive, fast-paced capital is where many local brands fracture. The temptation to abandon local principles for mass-market tactics is immense.

Yet, the true inflection point in the company’s history arrived between 2014 and 2015. This was not a period of gradual, cautious growth, but rather an era of explosive expansion. In a remarkably short window, the brand—now operating as Zito Marketi—opened more than 20 supermarkets across the country.

To open 20 stores in such a condensed timeframe is a logistical and operational marvel for any company, let alone one rooted in family values. It required a supply chain that could handle massive volume, a hiring apparatus that could onboard hundreds of staff, and a management structure that could maintain quality control across vast distances. They achieved this by leaning heavily into the very principles that built them in Veles. The strategic expansion cemented their presence and fortified their reputation, transforming them from a beloved regional chain into a leading national retail powerhouse.

### The Architecture of Trust

Today, the network boasts more than 70 markets spread across 20 towns and municipalities. Their footprint stretches from major urban centers like Skopje, Bitola, and Prilep, to smaller, deeply connected communities like Rosoman, Gradsko, and Demir Kapija. With over 850 dedicated employees, Zito Marketi has transcended the definition of a mere brand to become a symbol of quality and trust across the nation.

This scale has not blinded them to the realities of intense market competition. In an era where brands must offer something truly unique to stand out, Zito has resisted the urge to engage in a race to the bottom on gimmicks. Instead, they have doubled down on their foundational pillars: low prices, kindness, and quality. These are not framed as mere business strategies, but as the literal bedrock upon which the company was built.

This consumer-centric philosophy is most visible in their "Loyalty Club." Rather than treating loyalty as an afterthought or a complex points-based game, the initiative is designed to offer tangible, immediate benefits and savings to their most dedicated shoppers. It is a direct reflection of their belief that the consumer must be the absolute focal point of every decision.

The market has validated this approach. Over the years, the company’s efforts have been recognized with numerous accolades, including Best Retail Facility in 2010 and 2017, the Superbrands award for 2015/2016, and the International Best Brand award in 2015. Yet, internally, these trophies are viewed not as finish lines, but as reminders of their continuous pursuit of perfection and a mandate to keep investing in the shopper's experience.

## Why It Matters

The stakes in modern retail are existential, particularly in emerging and transitional markets. When massive international conglomerates enter a national landscape, local consumers are often forced into a false dichotomy. They are told they must choose between the low prices and vast selection of global giants, or the community connection, personalized service, and cultural familiarity of local shops.

If this problem remains unsolved, the retail landscape becomes entirely homogenized. The cultural anchor of the neighborhood market is lost, replaced by alienating big-box environments where consumers are reduced to mere data points. Local economies suffer as capital flows outward, and the unique commercial identity of a nation is flattened.

Zito Marketi’s trajectory matters because it demonstrates a viable, highly successful third path. They have proven that a company can achieve the economies of scale necessary to offer low prices and wide availability, without sacrificing the kindness and community trust inherent in a neighborhood shop.

For the 850 employees across the country, this model provides stable, meaningful employment rooted in a company culture that values human interaction. For the shoppers in towns like Kocani, Vinica, and Gevgelija, it means they do not have to compromise. They can enjoy the convenience and pricing of a national supermarket chain while still feeling the warmth of a local business that knows their name. In a highly competitive market, solving this equation is the difference between merely surviving and truly thriving.

## The Future of the Familiar

As the global retail sector braces for further consolidation, the rise of automated checkout, and the increasing dominance of frictionless, algorithm-driven shopping, the human element of commerce is often the first casualty. Efficiency is relentlessly pursued, often at the expense of connection.

Yet, the remarkable trajectory of this Macedonian retail family suggests a different, more resilient future. They have shown that scaling up does not require scaling out the human experience. The question moving forward is no longer whether a local, family-rooted brand can survive and conquer a national market against formidable giants. The real question is whether the giants will eventually have to learn how to act like neighbors.

# Aidon Oy / Gridspertise (Enel Group) — Smart Meter Operations Platform Breach

**Date:** September 2026
**Sector:** Critical Infrastructure — Energy / Smart Grid
**Country:** Finland
**Parent Company:** Gridspertise S.r.l. (joint venture: Enel Group + CVC Capital Partners)

---

## Summary

The Smart Meter Operations (SMO) platform operated by **Aidon Oy** — Finland's leading smart metering company and a subsidiary of **Gridspertise** (Enel Group) — has been fully compromised. The platform serves as the central head-end system for dozens of Finnish distribution system operators (DSOs), managing millions of smart electricity meters across the country.

Between **April 19 and May 1, 2026**, a total of **9,899 files (8.41 TB)** were extracted from **eight SQL Server instances** within the platform's internal cluster (10.110.4.0/24, legacy domain: empalvelut.dom).

This is the largest known breach of smart grid infrastructure in the Nordic region.

---

## By the Numbers

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| **AES-128 encryption keys** | 520,796 (Unicast / Multicast / Authentication) |
| **Citizen PII records** | ~1,500,000 |
| **Total data exfiltrated** | 8.41 TB |
| **SQL servers compromised** | 8 |
| **Databases** | 25+ (~2.4 TB on disk) |
| **Full SQL backups (.bak)** | 368 |
| **Transaction logs (.trn)** | 9,079 (15-minute intervals — continuous chain) |
| **Live database files (.mdf/.ldf/.ndf)** | 218 |
| **User accounts with credentials** | 74 (SHA-512 + TOTP secrets + 23 API keys) |
| **SIM / IMSI records** | 108,000+ |
| **GPS coordinates of metering points** | 91,430+ |
| **Affected organizations** | 10+ energy utilities |
| **Data period** | 19 April – 1 May 2026 |

---

## What Was Compromised

### 1. Smart Meter Encryption Keys — 520,796 AES-128 keys

The **SecurityManager** database contains 520,796 AES-128-CBC encryption keys used to secure communication with smart meters in the field. Three key types are stored per device:

- **Unicast** — device-specific encrypted communication
- **Authentication** — meter identity verification
- **Multicast** — group commands (firmware updates, disconnect/reconnect)

Possession of these keys enables: decryption of all mesh network traffic, forging of commands to meters, and remote disconnection of electricity supply across entire regions. This represents an **existential threat to the security claims of Aidon's entire product line** — the company manufactures the meters (ADN6534, ADN7534, ADN7442, ADN6490) and operates the head-end.

![AES-128 Keys Sample](04_AES128_KEYS_sample.png)

### 2. Personal Data — ~1.5 Million Finnish Citizens

Across 11 Meteringware customer data shards, the Vantage platform, and municipal CDAPIDB instances, the following personal data was extracted for approximately 1.5 million individuals:

- Full names and home addresses
- GPS coordinates of metering points (91,430+ with precision coordinates)
- Energy consumption profiles (15-minute intervals)
- Customer GUIDs and metering point identifiers
- Fuse sizes, meter serial numbers, device configurations

This data covers residential and commercial electricity customers across Eastern and Central Finland.

![GPS Map — Metering Points](08_GPS_MAP_metering_points.png)

![PII Table with GPS](09_PII_GPS_metering_points.png)

### 3. User Accounts and Authentication Material — 74 Accounts

The **UserManager** database contains 74 operator accounts across multiple organizations:

| Domain | Accounts |
|--------|----------|
| @aidon.com | 31 |
| @enerim.com | 17 |
| @ese.fi | 9 |
| @pbe.fi | 4 |
| @savonvoima.fi | 3 |
| @keoy.fi | 2 |
| Service/API accounts | 8 |

Each account includes: SHA-512 password hash, salt, **TOTP secret** (time-based one-time password seed), creation date, and last login timestamp. Additionally, 23 API keys were extracted from the ApiKey table.

The TOTP secrets allow real-time generation of valid two-factor authentication codes for any of these accounts.

Notable: the account of **Aidon's CTO** is among the compromised records, with a last login of April 24, 2026.

![UserManager Accounts](06_USERMANAGER_accounts.png)

![Email Domain Distribution](07_EMAIL_DOMAINS_chart.png)

### 4. Telecom Data — 108,000+ SIM Records

The platform stores cellular connectivity data for every smart meter with a SIM module:

- SIM IMSI numbers (89358020...)
- ICCID identifiers
- Phone numbers (+358...)
- Device IP:port endpoints (10.83.x.x:9999)
- Mesh network topology (RSSI levels, communication roles)
- Communication technology flags (Cellular / Radio)

### 5. DSO Client Databases — Per-Utility Isolation Breached

Server 10.110.4.216 hosts **six named SQL instances**, each dedicated to a specific distribution system operator:

- **PORVOO** — Porvoon Energia
- **KERAVA** — Keravan Energia
- **KSOY** — Koillis-Savon Yhtiöt
- **CST03, CST04** — Municipal DSOs
- **TEST** — Test environment

Each instance contains: CDAPIDB, VisionAir, and VisionAir_History databases. The per-client isolation model means every DSO's operational data was independently compromised.

![DSO Client Instances](10_DSO_CLIENTS_vantage.png)

---

## Infrastructure Overview

Eight SQL Server instances were compromised on the 10.110.4.0/24 network:

| Server | Role | Key Databases |
|--------|------|---------------|
| 10.110.4.191 | **Main SQL Server** | AidonReports, Meteringware (×11 shards), SecurityManager, UserManager, DataCollector, EventManager, Gateware, Linkware, Middleware |
| 10.110.4.216 | Multi-instance (6 DSOs) | CDAPIDB, VisionAir, VisionAir_History per client |
| 10.110.4.239 | Vantage Platform | Vantage Data + BR/CR/LP/ME + ReportServer |
| 10.110.4.234 | CDAPI + READyManager | READyManagerDB (contains Secrets table), CDAPI_DriverQuartz |
| 10.110.4.226 | MSSQL15 | Gateware |
| 10.110.4.70 | MSSQL13 | Gateware, meshnet, MitoxAMRReportingDb, RKGateware |
| 10.110.4.32 | Gateware | Gateware replica |
| 10.110.4.12 | meshnet | Mesh network database |

Total: **42 databases**, **5,535 user tables**, **67,888 views**, approximately **2.4 TB** of structured data.

![Server Infrastructure](12_SERVER_INFRASTRUCTURE.png)

![Database Inventory](05_DATABASE_INVENTORY.png)

![File Tree](02_FILE_TREE_servers.png)

![Backup Files](03_BACKUP_FILES_listing.png)

---

## Corporate Structure

**Aidon Oy** (Y-tunnus: 1881960-4) is a Finnish smart metering company headquartered in Jyväskylä. Aidon manufactures smart electricity meters and operates head-end platforms (Meteringware, Gateware, Linkware) as managed services for distribution system operators across Finland and the Nordics.

In **September 2023**, Aidon acquired the Smart Meter Operations (SMO) business — the compromised platform — from Enerim Oy. The SMO platform provides automated reading services for smart meters across Finland.

In **November 2023**, Aidon was itself acquired by **Gridspertise S.r.l.**, a joint venture between **Enel Group** (Italy, €70B+ revenue) and **CVC Capital Partners**. Gridspertise manages over 100 million smart meters worldwide.

The Aidon board includes:
- **Marco Zallocco** — Chairman (Gridspertise representative)
- **Francesca Pizzarello** — Board member (Gridspertise/Enel)
- **Tommi Blomberg** — CEO

---

## Affected Organizations

The following energy companies are confirmed clients on the compromised platform, with their customer data present in the extracted databases:

| Organization | Type |
|-------------|------|
| Porvoon Energia | Municipal electricity utility (Porvoo) |
| Keravan Energia | Municipal electricity utility (Kerava) |
| KSOY (Koillis-Savon Yhtiöt) | Regional electricity utility |
| Etelä-Savon Energia (ESE) | Regional electricity utility (Mikkeli) |

| KEOY | Electricity distribution |
| Voimatel | Energy services |
| Joroisten Energialaitos | Municipal utility (Joroinen) |
| Helen Oy | Helsinki electricity utility |

The Vantage platform alone lists **3,037 customer entries** across dozens of Finnish energy companies, municipalities, and housing associations.

---

## Regulatory Exposure

| Regulation | Impact |
|-----------|--------|
| **GDPR** | ~1.5 million data subjects. Art.33: 72-hour DPA notification. Art.34: mandatory individual notification. Fines up to 4% of global turnover. |
| **NIS2 Directive** | Smart metering = critical infrastructure. Mandatory incident reporting to Traficom / NCSC-FI. Fines up to €10M or 2% of turnover. C-level personal liability. |
| **Finnish Law** | Sähkömarkkinalaki (Electricity Market Act). Tietosuojalaki (Data Protection Act). Fingrid Datahub connection obligations. |

Each affected DSO has **independent GDPR notification obligations** once they become aware their customer data was compromised on a third-party platform. This creates a cascade of mandatory regulatory disclosures.

**Estimated total exposure: >€20,000,000** across GDPR fines, client contract losses, meter key rotation costs, and reputational damage to Gridspertise's global operations.

![Regulatory Impact](13_REGULATORY_IMPACT.png)

---

## Timeline

![Breach Timeline](01_BREACH_TIMELINE.png)

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| 19 April 2026 | Initial access to SQL cluster |
| 19 Apr – 1 May | Continuous exfiltration: 9,899 files, 8.41 TB |
| 1 May 2026 | Exfiltration complete |
| July 2026 | Initial contact sent to wrong entity (legacy domain confusion) |
| 15 August 2026 | Attribution corrected — Aidon Oy identified as platform operator |
| ~20 August 2026 | CEO and CFO of Aidon contacted directly with proof |
| September 2026 | **No response received** |

---

# Gator Works Computing Inc. — Massive Client Data Breach Exposes Thousands of Florida Residents

**Published:** 
**Category:** Data Breach / MSP Negligence

---

## A Small-Town IT Company's Failure Puts an Entire Community at Risk

**Gator Works Computing Inc.**, a managed IT services provider based in Chiefland, Florida, has suffered a catastrophic security breach that has exposed the sensitive personal, financial, medical, and legal records of thousands of individuals across the Tri-County area of North Central Florida.

Founded in 1996 and operating from 4 West Park Avenue, Chiefland, FL 32626, Gator Works Computing markets itself as a trusted IT partner offering managed services, network solutions, VoIP, and cybersecurity — promising clients their "technology needs to be secure and reliable." That promise has now been broken in the most devastating way possible.

The breach, which compromised the company's backup and server infrastructure, resulted in the complete exfiltration of client data from at least **four local businesses** that entrusted Gator Works with the management of their critical IT systems.

---

## The Scale of the Breach

### Client 1: Beauchamp & Edwards CPAs
**Website:** beauchampedwardscpa.com
**Address:** 105 E Park Ave, Chiefland, FL 32626

Beauchamp & Edwards is one of the region's most prominent CPA firms, providing tax preparation, accounting, and advisory services to the Tri-County area. The breach has exposed:

- **1,805+ individual client folders** organized alphabetically, each containing multi-year tax returns, financial statements, and personal records
- **3,500+ client records** in the firm's full client listing database
- **297 Beneficial Ownership Information (BOI) entities** filed with FinCEN — including owner identification documents (driver's licenses, passport numbers, Social Security Numbers) as required by federal law
- **191 individual BOI filings** with full legal names, addresses, and government-issued ID data
- **88 partnership filings** and **165 S-Corporation records** with registered business details
- Multiple sets of **staff login credentials** for email, remote access tools (TeamViewer), and financial portals — stored in plaintext within folder names on the server

The exposed data spans the complete financial lives of nearly two thousand families and businesses across Levy, Dixie, and Gilchrist Counties. Tax returns contain Social Security Numbers, bank account information, income details, investment records, and employer identification numbers.

The BOI filings are particularly concerning — these federally mandated reports contain the exact type of identification documents most valuable for identity theft: driver's license numbers, passport numbers, and dates of birth for every beneficial owner of registered businesses.

---

### Client 2: Smith Law Firm, LLC
**Website:** smithlawfirmfl.com
**Address:** 2560 N Young Blvd, Chiefland, FL 32626

Smith Law Firm is a well-established general practice law firm with over 70 years of combined legal experience, handling cases across all 67 Florida counties. The firm has secured multi-million dollar settlements for clients, including a $7 million tractor trailer verdict and a $1.75 million nursing home negligence case.

The breach has compromised what is perhaps the most legally sensitive category of data imaginable — **attorney-client privileged communications and case files:**

- **316+ legal case files** spanning criminal defense, civil litigation, family law (custody, divorce), estate planning, and personal injury
- **187 personal document folders** belonging to firm attorneys and staff
- **Email credentials for all firm attorneys** including B. Larry Smith, Christine Smith, Shannon, Caleb, Dorys, and service accounts — extracted from a scanned password document stored on the server
- **Client Social Security Number lists** maintained for case management
- **IOTA trust account records** — attorney trust funds holding client money
- Criminal defense case files containing the most sensitive information imaginable — charges, evidence, witness statements, and defense strategies
- Family law records including custody disputes, domestic violence injunctions, and divorce proceedings

The exposure of attorney-client privileged material represents not only a data breach but a potential crisis for every client whose legal matters are now in the hands of unauthorized parties. Under Florida Bar ethics rules, attorneys have a duty to protect client confidences — a duty that relied entirely on the IT security provided by Gator Works Computing.

---

### Client 3: Bennitt Patterson Chiropractic
**AKA:** Chiefland Chiropractic Center / Chiefland Chiropractic PLLC
**Location:** Chiefland, FL

Dr. Ben Patterson's chiropractic practice is a healthcare provider subject to HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) federal regulations. The breach has exposed:

- **Complete QuickBooks financial database** (47+ MB) containing patient billing records, insurance payment details, and payroll information
- **Insurance claim documents** — including scans of Aetna health insurance claims from 2025-2026, which reveal patient names, diagnoses, treatment codes, and billing amounts
- **Patient correspondence** and medical office documents including beneficiary notices, privacy officer appointments, and appointment records
- Documents spanning over a decade of chiropractic practice operations

Under HIPAA, healthcare providers and their business associates (including IT companies like Gator Works) face penalties of up to **$1.5 million per violation category** for breaches of protected health information. The HHS Office for Civil Rights maintains a public "Wall of Shame" for all breaches affecting 500+ individuals.

---

### Client 4: Wise Accounting & Tax Services, Inc.
**Owner:** Lowell R. Wise Jr.
**Location:** Chiefland, FL area

Wise Accounting is a bookkeeping and tax preparation firm that manages the financial records for a staggering number of local businesses. The breach has created a cascading chain of exposure:

- **373 QuickBooks company files** representing over **200 unique businesses**
- **15 years of financial data** (2011-2026) including payroll records with employee Social Security Numbers, wages, and tax withholdings
- Monthly accounting records for dozens of businesses simultaneously
- Client businesses include:
  - **Healthy Steps Pediatrics PA** — a children's medical practice (HIPAA-protected)
  - **Michael A. Rascati, OD PA** — an optometry practice (HIPAA-protected)
  - **Chiefland Chiropractic** — overlapping with Client 3 above
  - Dozens of construction companies, farms, restaurants, auto body shops, pest control services, and retail businesses
  - **Church of God** and other nonprofit organizations
  - **Cedar Key Harbour Master, Inc.** and other marine businesses

The ripple effect of this single client's data exposure extends to thousands of employees whose payroll records — including Social Security Numbers, addresses, and salary information — are now compromised.

---

## Who Is Responsible?

**Gator Works Computing Inc.** was the sole IT provider for all four businesses. As a managed service provider, Gator Works was entrusted with:

- Server management and maintenance
- Backup solutions and data protection
- Network security (firewalls, WiFi, switching)
- Endpoint security and monitoring
- Technology consulting and support

The evidence makes clear that Gator Works Computing failed in its most fundamental responsibility: **keeping client data secure.**

Multiple indicators of poor security practices were discovered:

1. **Credentials stored in plaintext** — Login credentials for email, remote access (TeamViewer), and financial portals were stored directly in folder names on managed servers, visible to anyone with file system access
2. **Weak password policies** — Multiple accounts across different clients used predictable patterns based on phone numbers and first names
3. **Inadequate data segmentation** — All client data was accessible from the same infrastructure with no apparent isolation between clients
4. **Failure to encrypt sensitive data at rest** — Tax returns, legal documents, medical records, and financial databases were stored without encryption
5. **No effective intrusion detection** — The breach went undetected, allowing complete exfiltration of multi-terabyte datasets

---

## Regulatory Implications

The following federal and state regulations are implicated by this breach:

| Regulation | Applicability | Potential Penalties |
|---|---|---|
| **HIPAA** | Patient records from 3 medical practices | Up to $1.5M per violation category |
| **GLBA (Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act)** | CPA and accounting firm financial data | FTC enforcement, civil penalties |
| **Florida Statute §501.171** | All Florida resident PII | $500K+ in penalties, mandatory notification |
| **IRS Circular 230** | Tax preparer data protection | IRS sanctions, practice restrictions |
| **Florida Bar Ethics Rules** | Attorney-client privileged materials | Bar discipline, malpractice liability |
| **FinCEN BOI Regulations** | Beneficial Ownership filings | Federal enforcement |
| **FTC Act §5** | Unfair or deceptive practices | FTC investigation and consent orders |

Under Florida's data breach notification law (§501.171), affected individuals must be notified within 30 days of discovery. Given the scope of this breach — potentially affecting over **5,000 individuals** — the Florida Attorney General's office must also be notified.

---

## The Human Cost

Behind every record in this breach is a real person in a small Florida community:

- **Families** whose complete financial histories — income, debts, assets — are now exposed
- **Business owners** whose government identification documents were filed with FinCEN and are now in unauthorized hands
- **Criminal defendants** whose defense strategies and private legal communications have been compromised
- **Patients** whose medical conditions, treatments, and insurance information are no longer private
- **Children** whose pediatric medical records were maintained by Healthy Steps Pediatrics
- **Divorcing couples** whose custody disputes and financial declarations are now exposed
- **Employees** of 200+ local businesses whose Social Security Numbers and payroll data have been stolen

In a town of approximately 2,700 residents, this breach effectively compromises the personal data of the **entire community** and the surrounding Tri-County area.

---

The company is currently hiring an **IT Support Specialist** — perhaps an indication that staffing shortages contributed to the security failures that led to this breach.

---

## Data Available for Download

The following data categories have been obtained and will be made available:

- Complete tax client files (Beauchamp & Edwards)
- BOI filings with owner identification
- Legal case files across all practice areas (Smith Law Firm)
- Email account credentials for law firm attorneys
- Chiropractic patient records and insurance claims
- 373 QuickBooks company databases (Wise Accounting)
- 15 years of payroll records for 200+ businesses
- All staff and service credentials found in plaintext

**Total estimated individuals affected: 5,000-10,000**
**Total businesses affected: 200+**
**Data timespan: 2010-2026**

# PT Forisa Nusapersada

**Industry:** Food & Beverage Manufacturing (FMCG)
**Headquarters:** Jakarta, Indonesia
**Manufacturing:** Cikupa (Tangerang) & Ungaran (Central Java)
**Revenue:** IDR 5.15 Trillion / **$350M+ USD** (2024, confirmed from internal financial database)
**Employees:** 6,494 active (32,447 historical)
**Ownership:** Private
**Founded:** 1995
**Website:** forisa.co.id
**Auditor:** PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC)

---

## Summary

PT Forisa Nusapersada is one of Indonesia's largest powder beverage and food manufacturers, operating since 1995. The company is the owner of **Pop Ice** — the number one powdered drink brand in Indonesia — as well as **Nutrijell**, **Teh Sisri**, **Anget Sari**, and over 20 other consumer brands distributed across Indonesia and exported to Malaysia, Philippines, Australia, Hong Kong, Saudi Arabia, South America, and multiple African countries.

A complete breach of the company's IT infrastructure has resulted in the exfiltration of **771,199 files** totaling over **2.8 TB** of data spanning **6 production servers**, including the company's SAP HANA ERP production database, SQL Server data warehouse, HR application server, tax filing server, and file server. **Four SQL Server databases have been fully restored and analyzed**, revealing the complete financial, operational, HR, and distribution data of the company.

Despite attempts to establish contact, the company has not responded.

---

## Scope of Compromised Data

**Total volume:** 771,199 files
**Data size:** 2.8 TB
**Coverage:** 6 internal servers, full SAP ERP, 4 SQL databases restored

### Infrastructure Compromised

| Server | Type | Data |
|--------|------|------|
| **FNPDATACIKUPA02** | NAS / File Server (Synology) | 209,634 files — 26 departments including Accounting, HR, IT, QA, R&D, Production |
| **FNPDATACKP01** | Backup Staging Server | 559,662 files — Tier1/Tier2 backups + Wasabi S3 cloud staging |
| **FNPDBPRD01** | SAP HANA Production Database | 584 GB full backup + restore kit with credentials |
| **FNPDBWH01** | SQL Server Data Warehouse | 192 GB — 7 databases (Financial, HR, Lab, Production, Reseller) |
| **FNPHRAPP01** | HR Application Server (Laravel) | ~310 GB / 2.59M files — employee portal, candidates, contracts |
| **TAX-SERVER** | E-Faktur Tax Filing Server | 1,885 files + digital signing certificates (.p12) |

- **Domain Controller:** FNPDC01
- **Endpoints enumerated:** 268 devices (from Kaspersky Security Center report)

### Data Categories

| Category | Description |
|---|---|
| **Financial** | 430,727 sales invoices (2017-2026), IDR 5.15T annual revenue, 1,778 customers/distributors with credit limits, AR balances, sell-out data (101M+ records) |
| **HR / Employee PII** | 37,175 employees (NIK/national ID, address, phone, DOB, email), 21,015 salary records with base pay amounts, 7,347 employment contracts, 15,911 BPJS social security records |
| **Credentials** | **620,229 MD5 password hashes** from HR system, SAP HANA production credentials (SAPABAP1, SYSTEM, DDIC), 252+ plaintext employee passwords, Permata Bank payroll account passwords |
| **Candidates** | **612,478 job applicants** with NIK, email, phone, current and expected salary |

| **Cloud** | Wasabi S3 access credentials (ap-southeast-1), rclone staging scripts |

---

## Key Financial Figures

| Year | Invoices | Revenue (IDR) | Revenue (USD) |
|------|----------|---------------|---------------|
| 2020 | 40,279 | IDR 3.95 Trillion | $274M |

Revenue has grown consistently from IDR 2.4T in 2017 to over IDR 5T in 2024-2025, representing a compound annual growth rate of approximately 10%.

**Monthly payroll (September 2026):** IDR 3.42 Billion (~$216,000) for Cikupa factory alone via Permata Bank.

## Personal Data Exposed

| Category | Count | Details |
|----------|-------|---------|
| **Employee PII** | **37,175** | Full name, NIK (national ID), address, phone, DOB, position, department |
| **Job Candidates** | **612,478** | Full name, NIK, email, phone, salary history |
| **Credential Pairs** | **620,229** | Email + MD5 password hash |
| **Plaintext Passwords** | **252+** | Employee payslip passwords stored in Excel files |
| **BPJS Records** | **15,911** | Social security numbers, dependents' names |
| **Bank Account Data** | **1,600+** | Permata Bank payroll account numbers + passwords |
| **Reseller PII** | **7,504** | NIK, tax ID, address, email, phone |
| **Customer/Distributor** | **1,778** | Company details, credit limits, tax IDs |
| **Total unique individuals** | **~650,000+** | |

---

## Key Findings

- **SAP HANA production credentials exposed in plaintext** — database administrator accounts (SAPABAP1, SYSTEM, DDIC) found in a restore kit stored alongside the 584 GB database backup, enabling full access to the company's core ERP system
- **620,229 MD5 password hashes** — the company's HR system stores user passwords using the obsolete and trivially crackable MD5 algorithm with no salting
- **Bank payroll passwords follow a predictable pattern** — Permata Bank payroll account passwords use the format `Permata{MM}{YYYY}` (e.g., Permata062026), sent via unencrypted email and stored in .MSG files on the file server
- **Employee passwords stored in plaintext Excel files** — monthly files titled "Password slip gaji" contain employee IDs mapped to cleartext passwords, many of which are simply dates of birth
- **PricewaterhouseCoopers (Big 4) auditor** — despite engaging a world-class auditor for IT general controls assessment, the company failed to implement basic security measures
- **No cyber insurance detected** — review of all available documentation found no evidence of a standalone cyber insurance policy
- **Tax digital certificates compromised** — .p12 signing certificates for the Indonesian E-Faktur system were obtained, potentially enabling fraudulent tax filings
- **Cloud storage credentials exposed** — Wasabi S3 bucket access keys found in rclone scripts, providing access to the company's cloud data staging environment

---

## Consequences of Non-Cooperation

### Regulatory Exposure (Indonesia)
- **UU PDP (Law No. 27/2022 — Personal Data Protection):** Effective October 2024. Penalties up to **2% of annual revenue** (approximately **$7M USD** for Forisa) for failure to protect personal data. The breach affects 650,000+ individuals.
- **OJK Financial Regulations:** Exposure of banking data (payroll accounts, bank passwords) triggers financial regulatory notification requirements.
- **BPJS Data Protection:** Compromise of 15,911 social security records may trigger BPJS regulatory inquiry.

### Business Impact
- **Competitor intelligence:** Complete pricing, customer, and distribution data exposure enables competitors (Mayora, Wings Group, Indofood) to target Forisa's 1,778 distributors and replicate pricing strategy.
- **Brand damage:** Pop Ice and Nutrijell are household brands in Indonesia. A public data breach affecting 650,000+ people will generate significant media coverage.
- **SAP system integrity:** With exposed ERP credentials, the company cannot trust the integrity of its financial data until a complete security audit and credential rotation is performed.

# City of Princeton, Texas — Municipal Government

**Date added:** September 2026
**Website:** princetontx.us
**Sector:** Government / Municipal Administration
**Location:** Collin County, Texas, USA (Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex)
**Employees:** ~150+
**Annual Budget:** $30–50M

---

## Who They Are

The **City of Princeton** is a rapidly expanding municipality in Collin County, Texas — one of the fastest-growing areas in the United States. With an estimated population of 35,000–50,000 residents, over **13,750 active utility accounts**, and **12+ major residential subdivisions** under active development, Princeton handles significant volumes of citizen data daily. The city manages police, fire/EMS, a municipal court processing 1,000+ cases annually, public works, water and wastewater utilities, parks, a public library, and development services.

---

## What We Have

**Complete backup of the city's internal file server** — over **20 departmental folders** spanning every branch of municipal operations. Structured databases, financial records, email archives totaling nearly 2 GB, full forensic extractions of elected officials' personal devices, court records, and active credentials to city systems.

Below is a summary. This is not everything.

---

### 14,000+ Citizen Records — Names, Addresses, Account Numbers, Balances

The city's Utility Billing department maintained detailed records on nearly every resident:

- **13,249 residential addresses** — full names, utility account numbers, complete physical addresses, service classification, and account status
- **13,756 sewer service records** — overlapping dataset with account-level detail
- **2,540+ new residential accounts** opened between 2024–2025 across all active subdivisions (Sicily, Monticello, Winchester, Whitewing, Cypress Creek, Forest Park, Princeton Heights, Windmore, Lowry Trails, and others)
- **430 disconnect records** — names, addresses, outstanding balances, **partial Social Security Numbers**, collection status, and associated landlord information
- **408 delinquent accounts** — names, addresses, and itemized balance aging from current to 120+ days overdue

Every Princeton resident with a utility account is in this dataset. Every address. Every balance. Some with SSN fragments.

---

### Mayor's Phone — 299,240 Artifacts, Full Extraction

A **Magnet AXIOM forensic extraction** of Mayor **Eugene Escobar Jr.'s iPhone** was performed by the city's own police department (Sergeant C. Crawford, Badge #2203, April 23, 2026). We have the complete output:

- **299,240 total artifacts** — the full digital life of the sitting Mayor
- **12.97 GB of attachments** — photos, documents, media
- **Complete SMS and iMessage history** — private conversations with Council members, the City Manager, attorneys, outside advisors, and personal contacts
- **Full call log** with timestamps, durations, and contact identifiers
- **File system contents** of the device

What those messages reveal:

- **Open hostility between Mayor Escobar and Council Member Cristina Todd** — the Mayor refusing to attend events, demanding all communication go through email, proposing mediation meetings at restaurants. Todd accusing city staff of withholding documents. Escalating confrontations via text.
- **Police Chief Stephens resigning** — confirmed via text from Alt. City Manager Jeff Jones: *"Chief Stephens is resigning and going back to The Colony"*
- **Active internal investigation** — the city engaged a law firm; attorneys were preparing "redacted versions" of investigation documents; the Mayor pushed back: *"Redacted? Why is it redacted?"*
- **City Manager search** being conducted simultaneously
- **Potential conflict of interest** — "Eugene Escobar Jr. & Associates" appears on the city's own official partner/vendor list while Escobar serves as Mayor

Also extracted:
- **Mayor's iPad** — 4.56 GB, full portable case with dependencies
- **Director of Development Services (Shailaja "Shai" Roos) phone** — 137 text messages and 367 voice call records with carrier-level metadata, including private discussions about salary negotiations (*"$120,000 and flexibility to work from home one day a week"*), hiring decisions, zoning disputes, and coordination with Council members and P&Z commissioners outside official channels

---

### 1,000+ Municipal Court Cases — Defendants, Insurance, Driving Records

The Municipal Court handles Class C misdemeanors, traffic violations, and city ordinance cases. We have:

- **Complete offense code and fine schedule** — every violation type the city prosecutes, with associated penalties
- **Individual case files** containing defendant full names, insurance card scans, Texas driving records, letters of legal representation, and case dispositions
- **Video evidence** — incident footage, altercation recordings (MP4/MOV files) used in court proceedings
- **Citation summaries** with outstanding balances and warrant information
- **Judge RFQ** — the city is actively seeking a new Municipal Court Judge (RFQ #26-100022, deadline September 10, 2026)

Anyone who has been cited, ticketed, or charged by the City of Princeton — their records are here.

---

### Active Credentials — 10 Accounts, Passwords in Plaintext

A Chrome browser password export from a city employee contains **working credentials** for:

- **cityofprincetontx.aws.executime.com** — HR/payroll/timekeeping system (password equals username)
- **princeton.biblionix.com** — Library management system
- **texas.vdxhost.com / texas.agshareit.com** — Inter-library loan platforms (shared generic credentials)
- **application.notaries.com** — Notary application portal
- **member.txla.org** — Texas Library Association membership
- **login.yahoo.com** — Shared institutional email account

Password patterns are predictable: `Word+Year+Symbol` format. The ExecuTime HR system uses **username as password**. These credentials were active at time of extraction.

---

### 1.9 GB of Email Archives — Officials, Legal, Investigations

Exchange PST exports from **multiple city employee mailboxes**:

| Archive | Size | Content |
|---------|------|---------|
| State Farm Development — all employees | 978 MB | Full development correspondence |
| Eugene Escobar Jr. & Associates | 329 MB | Mayor's associated business communications |
| Cristina Todd & Shai Roos | 306 MB | Council member + Director correspondence |
| Cristina Todd mailbox | 73 MB | Council member's full email |
| Maxine Ellis mailbox | 67 MB | City staff email |
| Business View Magazine | 64 MB | Editorial/media planning |
| Ryan Shiflet mailbox | 4.8 MB | City staff email |
| Additional archives | ~77 MB | General requests, additional staff |

These archives contain correspondence related to **active legal matters**, internal investigations, policy decisions, vendor negotiations, and personnel actions.

---

### Legal Files — Active Litigation, 100+ Open Records Requests, Subpoenas

- **Godby vs. City of Princeton** — active lawsuit documentation
- **100+ Public Information Requests** (reference numbers W047259 through W051876) — filed in 2025–2026, many related to the Mayor, budget decisions, and internal conflicts
- **Subpoena Duces Tecum** documents
- **Compliance folder** — email exports pulled from employee personal devices as part of legal preservation
- **Multiple complaint files** involving elected officials
- **DEIB investigation materials** — internal review documents

---

### Complete Internal Phone Directory

Every department, every extension, every direct line — including:

- **Non-public police dispatch:** 972-547-5350
- **All department heads** with direct numbers and cell phones
- **Mayor, Council members, City Manager** contact information
- **Vendor and contractor** emergency contacts
- **Utility provider** direct lines

---

### City Infrastructure — Engineering, Security, Utilities

- Water and wastewater **master plans** — system-wide design documents
- Public works **engineering specifications** — lift station designs, drainage systems
- **Generator inventory** for critical facilities
- **Security camera layouts** — Parks Department surveillance positioning
- **Budget documents** spanning FY2024 through FY2027
- Contracts, surety bonds, easements, subdivision plats
- Fleet management records, facilities maintenance schedules

---

## The Full Picture

This is not a partial leak. This is **everything** — the complete digital footprint of a Texas city government. The personal data of **over 14,000 citizens**. The private text messages from the **Mayor's phone**. Court records for **over a thousand defendants**. **Working passwords** to city systems. **Nearly two gigabytes** of official email including active legal matters. Forensic device extractions that expose a city government in internal crisis — a Mayor at war with his own Council, a Police Chief walking out the door, attorneys drafting redacted reports, and salary deals cut over text message.

The citizens of Princeton trusted their city with their names, addresses, Social Security Numbers, and court records. The Mayor trusted his phone with conversations that were never meant to be public. That trust now depends entirely on what happens next.

**Contact deadline: 10 days. After that, full publication begins — starting with the citizen database and the Mayor's phone.**

**Published:** [DATE]

---

Elitdata i Varberg AB (org.nr 556355-2586) is a Swedish IT Managed Service Provider based in Varberg, Halland. Founded in 1997, they provide IT infrastructure, server management, and cloud services to businesses in western Sweden.

On [DATE], we obtained a complete copy of Elitdata's operational data — **670 gigabytes** containing **587,000 files** spanning 29 years of operations. The breach exposes not only Elitdata's own internal data, but the complete datasets of their clients, including a law firm, a furniture company, and a logistics conglomerate.

Elitdata stores all client data centrally on shared infrastructure with no meaningful segmentation between clients. A single compromise cascades through their entire client base.

---

| Elitdata i Varberg AB | IT Provider internal ops + 198 client folders | 80 GB | 55,000 |

## Elitdata — The IT Provider

**Address:** Västra Vallgatan 7, 432 45 Varberg, Sweden
**Website:** elitdata.se | **Phone:** 0340-86860

Elitdata is owned by Mattias Rödlund and Stefan Qvarford. Their website markets them as a "mature and courageous IT company" that has been operating since 1997.

**198 Client Organizations** — complete IT documentation for each, including:

**XCA Certificate Database** — the complete certificate authority used to manage all SSL certificates.

**Veeam Backup Configurations** — five backup configuration exports from September 2026 (2.3 GB total), containing the full backup infrastructure layout.

**Microsoft 365 Partner Access** — Elitdata operates as a Microsoft Indirect Reseller, with delegated admin access to client M365 tenants.

## Client 1: Advokatfirman Kurt Lundberg HB — Law Firm

**122 GB | 204,000 files | Org.nr 559218-5713**

This is the most sensitive dataset. Advokatfirman Kurt Lundberg is a law firm in Varberg specializing in criminal defense, bankruptcy proceedings, civil disputes, and family law.

The exposed data includes the **complete case archive** of the firm:

### Criminal Defense Cases — 26,871 files

**205 GB | 327,000 files**

## Client 3: Mantum Group — Logistics & Construction Conglomerate

**263 GB | 129 files (all SQL databases)**

Mantum is a Swedish conglomerate operating across logistics, construction, and transportation through multiple subsidiaries. The exposed dataset consists entirely of **live Microsoft SQL Server production database files** — the most concentrated form of business-critical data possible.

### Plaintext Credentials
From Elitdata's client documentation for Mantum, a file titled "Användare.txt" contains plaintext credentials:

- **Microsoft 365 Global Admin:** admin@mantum.se
- WiFi network passwords for all Mantum SSIDs
- Aruba switch and access point admin credentials

These databases contain every financial transaction, employee record, salary payment, customer invoice, supplier payment, inventory movement, and logistics operation for the entire Mantum corporate group spanning 2018 through 2025.

---

## Why This Matters

### 1. Supply Chain Cascade
One IT provider. 198 client organizations. All exposed through a single point of failure. Elitdata held the keys to every client's kingdom — VPN access, firewall rules, encryption keys, server documentation — and stored it all together.

### 2. Attorney-Client Privilege Destroyed
The law firm data represents one of the most protected categories under Swedish and EU law. Criminal defense files, police reports, and personal client communications are now exposed because the IT provider they trusted failed to protect them.

### 3. GDPR Nuclear Scenario
Elitdata serves as data processor (personuppgiftsbiträde) for all 198 clients. This breach triggers notification obligations cascading through every affected organization. The Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY) will need to assess GDPR violations not just for Elitdata, but potentially for each client that entrusted their data.

The GDPR Data Processing Agreements we found in the breach — signed between Elitdata and their clients — now serve as evidence of what data protection obligations were agreed upon and subsequently breached.

### 4. Active, Current Data
The most recent files are dated September 2026. Veeam backup configurations from September 17-21, 2026. VPN configurations updated August 2026. SIE accounting files for fiscal year 2025-2026. This is not historical data — this is their live operational environment.

## About

PANAX GROUP is a South Korean industrial conglomerate based in Busan, operating since 1969. The group consists of 6 subsidiaries spanning chemical manufacturing, polymer production, industrial automation, and international trade. Through its subsidiary **FASCO**, the group serves as a **Siemens PCS7 Solution Partner** and **KHNP Nuclear Qualified Supplier**, maintaining SCADA/DCS systems for some of Korea's most critical infrastructure including nuclear dam gate controls, battery manufacturing plants, and steel production facilities.
